ruling.recommended_action: No refund of excess distance fare (segment covered by rider's named-road consent to Halus Link); send driver nothing further — no violation recorded. Note on the record that the call was made and logged; no reminder needed.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat F7/F8, driver statement F9 and the complaint contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the stated facts are a traffic jam, a phone call and a fare dispute. safety_concern = none.

Route deviation: actual 11.7 km vs optimal 9.8 km = +1.9 km [F1], over the 1 km tolerance of RD-1, so the case is in the refund matrix. Only one off-route segment was logged [F3]: 10:06–10:11, 3.21 km vs 1.50 km optimal, +1.71 km, roads driven … PUNGGOL EAST → PUNGGOL CENTRAL → PASIR RIS INDUSTRIAL DRIVE 1 → HALUS LINK.

Consent / RD-5: before the segment began (call logged 09:56, segment 10:06–10:11) the driver called and said "Accident on Tampines Expressway ahead, ok if I go round via Halus Link?"; the rider answered "Ok, can, go ahead" [F8]. This is a recorded call (F8 transcript; corroborated by F9), satisfying RD-5's requirement that verbal notice be evidenced by the call recording, and it preceded the deviation. It is a clean, unqualified agreement to a named road — Halus Link — not a qualified yes, and the segment actually drove HALUS LINK [F3], so the named-road consent covers that segment including the connecting roads onto it and off it (RD-5 / RD-3). RD-3 likewise exempts a rider-accepted route. The traffic condition underlying the reroute is independently verified: the accident at 09:47 was 0 m from the optimal route (which uses Tampines Expressway) with Tampines Expressway at speed band 1 through 10:11 [F10, F13, F11]. Consent, not the traffic reason, is what exempts the segment here, so RD-4's general non-exemption of a traffic reason does not bite — the rider's own agreement does.

Refund arithmetic: deviation 1.9 km − 1.71 km exempt = 0.19 km refundable. At this trip's per-km distance fare of $1.4104/km [F4] that is $0.27, and the billed excess is $2.65 [F4]. However, RD-1's second sentence is explicit that departures under 0.2 km are map-matching noise, and the residual 0.19 km falls under that threshold; accordingly the amount refundable is $0.00. Under RD-2 the segment is exempt, so no partial refund of excess distance fare is due and no driver violation is recorded (contrast the "no traffic reason" row, which is not this case). The total charged $27.10 [F6] was computed at 1.0× surge [F5], so no SURGE-2 differential arises. Rider profile [F15] and driver profile [F16] (route upheld: 0) are not used to decide anything, and RD-6's flag is not triggered — the driver has no upheld route deviation; the general dispute count is not a route-deviation flag basis.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS distance and segment [F1, F3], fare build-up [F4, F6], the timestamped call with transcript [F8], and traffic data [F10, F13] cover every element. Amount $0.00 is under $10 and route deviation is decided by the system following DISP-001 (TH-1/TH-2, C1); precedent DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute, $3.20) is distinguishable because here the rider was informed and agreed on a recorded call.

segment_findings.reason: The driver's call at 09:56, before the 10:06–10:11 segment, proposed going round via Halus Link and the rider answered "Ok, can, go ahead" — a recorded, unqualified agreement to a named road (RD-5, evidenced by the call recording per RD-5 system detail; RD-3 rider-accepted route). The segment drove HALUS LINK [F3], so the named road is present and covers the segment, including the connecting roads onto it. The underlying accident on Tampines Expressway (0 m from the optimal route, band 1 through 10:11) is verified [F10, F13], but exemption rests on the rider's own consent before the segment, not on RD-4.

element_findings.element: RD-5 notice and rider consent to the deviation (recorded call before segment)
element_findings.reason: Call at 09:56, answered, 40 s, transcript shows the driver naming the reason (accident on Tampines Expressway) and the route (via Halus Link) and the rider agreeing in her own words; the segment began at 10:06, so notice and consent preceded it. Driver's later statement [F9] merely corroborates and is not relied on alone.

element_findings.element: RD-1 residual deviation above the exempt segment vs the 0.2 km map-matching noise floor
element_findings.reason: 1.9 km total deviation − 1.71 km exempt segment = 0.19 km, under the 0.2 km noise threshold, so nothing is refundable and no violation is recorded.
Multiplier was 1.0× — no surge applied and no differential exists, so the surge notice rules are not in issue.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's phone call before pickup was answered and she agreed to the Halus Link route [F8]; on the recorded call the named road was actually driven [F3], so the off-route segment is exempt under RD-5/RD-3 and the excess distance fare ($2.65) is not refundable. The only non-exempt remainder (0.19 km ≈ $0.27) falls under RD-1's 0.2 km noise floor.
Not used as the basis for consent: a driver's account of verbal agreement is a claim, not consent; the basis is the recorded call transcript in F8.
